changes_made.explanation: Normalized task names to title case and removed redundant/overly broad task descriptions. Added 'Comment-Edit Alignment' as a core task studied in the paper.

Changed answer from 'No' to 'Yes' since the paper extensively uses precision, recall, and F1 scores to evaluate comment-edit alignment. Removed metric variants (micro-F1, macro-F1, AO-F1) as they are just specific forms of F1 measurement.
No LLMs were used as judges/evaluators in this paper. GPT-4 was used as a generation model, not for evaluating outputs after generation.

guideline: Experts evaluated edits using a rubric with specific factors: Compliance (1-3 scale), Promises (true/false), Paraphrases (true/false), Technical details (true/false), and comprehensiveness comparisons

changes_made.explanation: Normalized criteria to lowercase for consistency. Added 'comprehensiveness' as an explicit evaluation criterion used in the human evaluation. Consolidated duplicate criteria.

overall_notes: The paper focuses on scientific paper revision tasks using the ARIES dataset. It evaluates both comment-edit alignment (classification task) and edit generation (NLG task). The automatic evaluation uses standard precision/recall/F1 metrics, and human evaluation uses a detailed rubric. The extraction was generally accurate but needed normalization and some corrections to task descriptions and metrics.
